finding.claim: The icon URL is stored without any validation and later fetched by the nightly sync job. A user who can call PUT /profile can make the server send GET requests to arbitrary URLs, including internal hosts, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints. The response body is read into a byte array.

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives the user-controlled icon
this.iconUrl = icon is stored with no scheme, host, or IP check
the nightly sync() fetches URI.create(iconUrl) with an HTTP GET (second-order path)

finding.guards_checked: Only `webhook` is validated, by a regex at line 12. `icon` has no allowlist, scheme check, or host/IP check. The HttpClient is passed in and its configuration is not visible. The Java default is not to follow redirects, which does not help here because the initial URL is already unrestricted. I did not see an egress filter in the code.

verdict.guard_found: none (only webhook is regex-validated at src/Profile.java:12; icon is unchecked)
verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the user-supplied `icon` unvalidated and src/Profile.java:23 fetches it with GET via URI.create(iconUrl), and no scheme, host or IP guard exists anywhere in the code.
